column2: Nav2 costmap_2d plugins: ObstacleLayer and VoxelLayer, configured via observation_sources in the costmap YAML. Key terms: sensor_msgs/PointCloud2 or LaserScan topics, subscription via rclcpp/nav2 message filters (tf2_ros::MessageFilter), observation buffers, marking and clearing, obstacle_range, raytrace_range, min_obstacle_height, max_obstacle_height, frame_id, transform tolerance, Layer::onInitialize, declareParameter, and nav2_costmap_2d::Costmap2D grid cells with LETHAL_OBSTACLE.

Nav2 StaticLayer subscribes to the map topic via a rclcpp/nav2_util subscription (create_subscription<nav_msgs::msg::OccupancyGrid>) using a QoS profile with transient_local durability, a map_topic parameter, a callback storing the map, and a use_maximum or track_unknown_space setting; it then updates the costmap via onInitialize, matchSize, and updateBounds/updateCosts, with lifecycle node handling and mutex protection.

Key concepts: Nav2 costmap layer lifecycle (onInitialize, activate, deactivate, reset, onFootprintChanged); lifecycle nodes and LifecycleNode states (inactive, active); rclcpp subscriptions created in onInitialize versus activation; resetting or destroying subscriptions in deactivate; the ROS 2 managed lifecycle transitions; the nav2_util::LifecycleNode; callback group management; the mutex or rclcpp::SubscriptionOptions for thread safety; and the isActive/enabled flag guarding callbacks.

Key concepts: multiple rclcpp subscriptions per plugin node, storing subscriber shared_ptrs as class members, callback groups and executor threading, message_filters for time synchronization (ApproximateTime/ExactTime policies), QoS profiles (rclcpp::QoS, transient_local for maps, sensor_data for scans), onInitialize lifecycle and activate/deactivate/reset handling, thread safety with mutexes, and topic remapping via parameters.

MoveIt2 move_group capabilities (move_group capabilities parameter, plugin-based capability loading such as MoveGroupPickPlaceAction, ExecuteTaskSolutionCapability), launch file parameters and arguments, ROS 2 launch Python (generate_move_group_launch, DeclareLaunchArgument, Node parameters), robot_description and SRDF, pull request changes, version compatibility, deprecated or renamed capability plugins, and move_group default capabilities.

MoveIt2 launch configuration: move_group capabilities, the 'capabilities' launch argument, moveit_config.move_group_capabilities, MoveItConfigsBuilder, generate_move_group_launch / move_group.launch.py, plugin loading (move_group_capabilities parameter), default vs. custom capabilities such as MoveGroupExecuteService and MoveGroupKinematicsService, ROS 2 launch arguments, parameter files, and troubleshooting missing or misconfigured capability plugins.

Key concepts: ROS 2 launch arguments (DeclareLaunchArgument), default values and required arguments, LaunchConfiguration substitution, and how unset arguments cause errors or empty parameters. Also relevant: MoveIt2 move_group launch generation (generate_move_group_launch, move_group_capabilities in MoveItConfigsBuilder), the move_group node's capabilities parameter, plugin loading via pluginlib, and how an empty or missing capabilities string affects which move_group plugins load.

Gazebo plugin Configure() receives sdf::ElementPtr _sdf and EntityComponentManager; typically reads topic names from SDF tags (e.g., <topic>, <robotNamespace>), builds a transport::Node or gz::transport::Node, and calls Advertise<gz::msgs::Double>() or similar to create a publisher. Key terms: ISystemConfigure, gz-sim/ignition-gazebo, Model/Link entities, rotor joint, velocity command, namespace prefixing, MotorSpeed message, sdf parameters, pub/sub, Publisher.

Key concepts: Gazebo Transport (gz::transport::Node), Publisher advertised via node.Advertise<T>(topic), protobuf message types (e.g., gz.msgs.Actuators or Double/Vector messages), publishing with publisher.Publish(msg), topic naming with robot namespace, ModelPlugin/Configure/PreUpdate lifecycle, multicopter motor speed commands, rotor velocity arrays, MulticopterMotorModel, and the ignition/gz-sim plugin interface.

Key concepts: Gazebo Transport/ECM (EntityComponentManager) and PreUpdate/PostUpdate callbacks; Actuators component (gz::msgs::Actuators, velocity array); rotor velocity computation from twist commands via allocation matrix or motor model; first-order lag/filtering; publishing via gz::transport Node::Advertise and Publish each update; components SetComponentData/ChangedComponent; thread-safety with mutexes; simulation time and delta time; Configure, PreUpdate, PostUpdate lifecycle.

CMakeLists.txt changes for Gazebo plugins: find_package(gz-sim, gz-plugin, gz-msgs, gz-transport, gz-math, Protobuf), add_library as a shared MODULE, target_link_libraries with gz-sim/gz-msgs/gz-transport/gz-plugin targets, set C++ standard (C++17), install targets to the lib directory, set GZ_SIM_SYSTEM_PLUGIN_PATH, and link with include directories and pkg-config dependencies.

Key concepts: Gazebo Sim (gz-sim) system plugins, the Configure(Entity, shared_ptr<EntityComponentManager>, EventManager, EntityComponentManager) callback, sdf::ElementPtr SDF parsing, _sdf->HasElement() and _sdf->Get<std::string>("topic", default) for reading tags, plugin parameters such as <command_sub_topic>, <robotNamespace>, and <rotor_count>, default fallback values, gz::transport Node subscriptions, and the model's scoped topic naming convention.

MultiThreadedExecutor (rclcpp::executors::MultiThreadedExecutor) in ROS2 C++; rclcpp::init, node creation via std::make_shared<Node>, executor.add_node(), executor.spin(), rclcpp::shutdown(). Callback groups (MutuallyExclusive vs Reentrant), number_of_threads option, std::thread concurrency, Python rclpy.executors.MultiThreadedExecutor with ExternalShutdown and spin, and executor.remove_node cleanup.

Key concepts: rclcpp::executors::MultiThreadedExecutor, the executor.add_node() method, creating a node via std::make_shared, calling executor.spin() in main, rclcpp::init and rclcpp::shutdown, callback groups (MutuallyExclusive vs Reentrant), the num_threads parameter, image subscriptions (sensor_msgs/msg/Image, cv_bridge, image_transport), and using a reentrant callback group for concurrent image processing.

Callback groups in ROS2: MutuallyExclusiveCallbackGroup (default, callbacks run serially) versus ReentrantCallbackGroup (callbacks may run concurrently). Assign image subscriptions/timers to a ReentrantCallbackGroup, pass it via callback_group argument, use MultiThreadedExecutor with num_threads, and consider rclpy/rclcpp threading, executor spin, and parallel processing of image data.

Key concepts: callback groups in ROS2 (MutuallyExclusiveCallbackGroup and ReentrantCallbackGroup), passing the callback_group argument to create_subscription() in rclpy or rclcpp, creating the group with node.create_callback_group() or a direct constructor, executor thread scheduling, mutual exclusion versus parallel execution, and assigning subscriptions and timers to groups before adding the node to a MultiThreadedExecutor.

Callback groups decide which callbacks may run concurrently in ROS2. Mutually exclusive groups (the default) allow only one callback at a time, while reentrant groups permit parallel execution. The executor (MultiThreadedExecutor, SingleThreadedExecutor) schedules ready callbacks across its thread pool, respecting group constraints. Key terms: callback group, mutually exclusive, reentrant, thread pool, ready queue, node.create_callback_group, subscription options.

Serial communication (UART/USB serial) between Arduino Mega and a ROS 2 host, rosserial-style protocols, micro-ROS and micro-ROS agent, DDS and XRCE-DDS, serial transport, baud rate, packet framing and checksums, custom message serialization, Python or C++ serial bridge nodes, topics, publishers and subscribers, and alternatives such as Micro-ROS on ESP32 or Raspberry Pi bridges.

Key concepts: ROS 2 nodes, topics, publishers and subscribers; micro-ROS and rosserial for microcontrollers; Arduino Mega serial (UART) communication; baud rates, serial ports and USB-to-serial adapters; message serialization and custom message types; Python serial libraries such as pyserial; launch files and package structure; example repositories, setup instructions and troubleshooting.

Key concepts: USB serial connection between Arduino Mega and host PC; Arduino sketch using Serial.begin with matching baud rate; serial port device paths (/dev/ttyACM0 or /dev/ttyUSB0) and permissions (dialout group); ROS 2 workspace and node setup; serial_server and virtual_serial_client nodes; message formats and topics; pyserial library; ROS 2 distribution sourcing; colcon build; launch files.

Serial link limitations: low bandwidth and baud rate settings, latency, no built-in message framing or checksums, buffer overflow on the Arduino's small RAM, blocking reads, USB/UART port naming and permissions, single-master topology, timing jitter, lack of QoS and ROS 2 DDS integration, and need for custom protocol design and error handling.

Key concepts: rclcpp::Subscription, create_subscription templated on message type, callback signatures, std::bind with placeholders (_1), lambda captures ([this, extra]), std::function, boost::bind, member function callbacks, SharedPtr message parameters, QoS settings, callback groups, and passing additional context or state to subscriber callbacks.

Key concepts: shared_ptr ownership and lifetime; std::make_shared and rclcpp::spin with node shared_ptr; weak references and captures like [this] versus capturing shared_ptr; subscription handles (rclcpp::Subscription::SharedPtr) stored as member variables; object destruction and dangling pointers; callback groups; rclcpp::shutdown; keeping nodes alive during spin; RAII and scope.

Key concepts: RCLCPP_INFO logging macro, rclcpp::Node::get_logger(), lambda captures ([this], [&], by-value captures), accessing the node's logger inside a lambda versus a member function, stream-style versus printf-style formatting, a Node member function or this pointer, captured variables in callbacks, std::bind alternative, rclcpp subscription callback signature, and thread-safety considerations when logging from callbacks.

Key concepts: rclcpp::Subscription shared pointers as node members; one member per subscription (e.g., subscription_a_, subscription_b_); create_subscription<MsgType>(topic, queue_size, callback); lambda captures (capture by value or this) to bind distinct extra arguments; std::bind alternative; subscription lifetime tied to node; callback groups and executors; topic names and QoS settings; RCLCPP_INFO with get_logger().

Key concepts: ROS2 rclcpp create_subscription() signature; the QoS argument (queue depth given as an integer, e.g., 10, or rclcpp::QoS(depth)); std::bind with placeholders (std::placeholders::_1) for the message argument; the order of arguments (topic name, QoS, callback); std::bind(&Class::method, this, _1, extra args); KeepLast history policy and queue depth; deprecated bind versus lambda usage.

Controller manager update loop; update_rate parameter (Hz); read() and write() hardware interface methods called each cycle; period/dt passed to read/write; control loop timing; real-time thread; hardware component lifecycle; SystemInterface and ActuatorInterface; command and state interfaces; controller update() and chained controllers; jitter and cycle time; sampling rate versus update frequency.

Key concepts: controller_manager update rate, hardware component update_rate parameter, read()/write() cycle, rate divider/skipping logic in ResourceManager/ros2_control, ros2_control hardware interface lifecycle, periodic execution, jitter and timing accuracy, real-time thread scheduling, controller update() vs hardware read/write, sampling and aliasing, mismatched rates causing skipped or repeated cycles, timing drift, and cycle-time overruns.

Key concepts: ros2_control hardware interface lifecycle (read/update/write cycle), controller manager update rate, hardware update rate and loop counter, command interfaces and state interfaces, command buffering or double buffering, real-time safe lock-free queues or realtime buffers (realtime_tools RealtimeBuffer), setpoint synchronization, jitter and latency, timestamps, interpolation, trajectory sampling, and deterministic write() timing.

colcon build copies files into install space; without --symlink-install, install/ holds copies, so edits to Python launch files require rebuilding (colcon build) or reinstalling the package. Key terms: colcon build, install space, copy vs symlink, ament_python, setup.py/data_files, launch files, rebuild, source install/setup.bash, editable installs.

Key concepts: colcon build and install space, --symlink-install (symlinks to source files), ros2 launch resolving files from the install share directory, the difference between Python launch files and modified C++ or entry-point code, changed package.xml or setup.py requiring rebuild, launch file location via get_package_share_directory, and caveats such as new files, renamed files, or non-symlinked resources needing rebuild or re-sourcing setup.bash.

PlotJuggler, ROS2 bag files (rosbag2, MCAP/SQLite3), nav_msgs/Odometry topics, pose and twist fields, position x/y/z, quaternion orientation and Euler conversion, timestamps and time synchronization, plotting time series, XY trajectory plots, multi-topic overlay, reference versus estimated trajectories, ground truth alignment, SE(3) error metrics such as ATE and RPE, and plugin-based data loading.

PlotJuggler setup for ROS2 bags: installation via apt (ros-<distro>-plotjuggler-ros) or source build, sourcing the ROS2 workspace, rosbag2 formats (sqlite3 and mcap plugins), ros2 bag play for live replay, topic subscription, time synchronization and use_sim_time, message field navigation, layout saving, and common troubleshooting for missing plugins or dependencies.

PlotJuggler XY plot mode, plotting one field against another, selecting x-axis series and y-axis series, multiple odometry topics (nav_msgs/Odometry pose.pose.position x and y), drag-and-drop time series into XY view, curve overlay and legend, topic/field paths, ROS2 bag playback, trajectory comparison, axis-aligned path plotting, and reference frames or coordinate alignment across odometry sources.

PlotJuggler custom functions and transforms (Lua scripting), time-series math and derived series, cross-topic synchronization and resampling, XY plot mode, reference trajectory comparison, Euclidean distance and positional error computation, timestamp alignment and interpolation, plot annotations, markers, and tooltips, ROS2 odometry (nav_msgs/Odometry) pose fields, and exporting computed error values.

ros2_control hardware interface description: URDF/xacro <ros2_control> tags with <hardware> plugin, <joint>, <gpio> elements, <param> and <state_interface>/<command_interface> definitions; hardware_interface::HardwareInfo and ComponentInfo structures; component_parser.hpp (hardware_interface parsing utilities like parse_control_resources_from_urdf); controller_manager loading; resource_manager; URDF parsing in C++ via urdf/tinyxml2; SystemInterface, SensorInterface, ActuatorInterface.

Relevant material would cover the hardware_interface::parse_control_resources_from_urdf() function in component_parser.hpp, which parses ros2_control URDF tags (<ros2_control>, <hardware>, <joint>, <sensor>, <gpio>, <plugin>, command and state interfaces). It depends on the hardware_interface package and tinyxml2, not the controller_manager node. Key terms: ComponentInfo, HardwareInfo, InterfaceInfo, URDF string parsing, resource manager, and the ros2_control plugin/pluginlib system.

Key concepts: ros2_control's hardware_interface package, component_parser.hpp header (resource_manager/urdf parsing utilities), ros2_control_plugins and ament_cmake dependencies, C++ header-only usage versus linking to hardware_interface library, Apache License 2.0 licensing, URDF/xacro ros2_control tags (<ros2_control>, <hardware>, <gpio>, <param>), transmission and joint interfaces, package.xml and CMake find_package dependencies, and the tinyxml2 parsing dependency.

Step-down (buck) DC/DC converter, input 18V, regulated output 12V and 6V, efficiency, power dissipation, heat, linear regulator vs switching regulator, voltage divider and resistor drop, load current, constant output under varying load, pulse-width modulation, inductor, diode, capacitor filtering, battery life, thermal management, ripple, power rating.

Key concepts: DC/DC buck converter specifications (input voltage range, maximum continuous output current, efficiency, load regulation), motor stall and inrush current, peak versus continuous current ratings, battery voltage variation (fully charged 18V+ and under load), regulated 5V/6V/12V outputs for Arduino and motors, thermal derating and heatsinking, input/output capacitors, reverse polarity and overcurrent protection, fuses, and common ground wiring for noise

Key concepts: DC/DC converter topology (buck/step-down switching regulator), output voltage regulation and feedback loop, load regulation, line regulation, output current rating, current limiting and overcurrent protection, thermal shutdown, efficiency, input voltage range, inductor and capacitor filtering, transient response, dropout voltage, and maximum load current specifications.

Key concepts: feedback voltage divider, trim/adjust pin, reference voltage (typically 0.5-0.6V, e.g., 0.59V for the SparkFun part), setpoint resistor between Trim and GND, output voltage formula Vout = Vref × (1 + R_upper/R_lower), resistor tolerance and power rating, E-series resistor values, input range limits, dropout voltage, thermal limits, and load regulation.

Obstacle avoidance and collision detection in mobile robots: range sensors (ultrasonic, infrared, LiDAR, depth cameras), distance thresholds, safety zones and stop distance, braking and deceleration, emergency stop logic, sensor polling and filtering, finite state machines, and reactive control loops.

Key concepts: the Nav2 Collision Monitor, configured via YAML parameters under the collision_monitor node; polygons (PolygonStop, PolygonSlow) with types such as "stop", "slowdown", "approach" and point/velocity limits; observation sources (scan, pointcloud) with topics, min_points, and frames; base_frame_id, cmd_vel_in/out topics; launch files, example params.yaml, and tutorials in the navigation2 repository.

Nav2 Collision Monitor concepts: polygon shape and points defining the stop zone's extent, action_type (stop, slowdown, approach), min_points threshold, observation sources (scan, pointcloud) with topic and min_height/max_height, base_frame_id and transform_tolerance, and velocity limits for approach-based stopping such as time_before_collision, simulation_time_step, and robot footprint dimensions.

ros_gz_bridge connects ROS 2 and Gazebo Transport topics via parameter bridge configuration (topic name, message type, direction). Key terms: Gazebo Fortress vs Garden (Ignition vs gz-transport versions), ROS 2 distros (Humble, Iron, Rolling), ros_gz package versions matching Gazebo release, gz-msgs/gz-transport, message type mapping (ros_gz_interfaces), bridge direction ([, ], @), topic name remapping, and version incompatibility causing silent message loss.

Key concepts: ros_gz_bridge, Gazebo Transport vs. ROS 2 middleware (DDS), gz-transport and gz-msgs library versions, Gazebo Fortress (Ignition-era) and Garden releases, ABI/API compatibility, version-matched ros_gz packages, GZ_VERSION environment variable, topic name mapping and parameter_bridge configuration, message type mismatches, and troubleshooting with gz topic -l and ros2 topic list.

Key concepts: ros_gz_bridge build from source; ROS 2 Humble branch selection (ros_gz repository, humble branch); GZ_VERSION environment variable and Gazebo version matching (Fortress, Garden, Edifice); colcon build and rosdep dependencies; ros_gz_bridge parameter_bridge topic mapping between ROS 2 and Gazebo Transport; message type compatibility; sourcing the workspace; troubleshooting message publishing and topic verification with ros2 topic echo.

Key concepts: ROS 2 subscription callbacks; message types as std::shared_ptr<const MsgT> (or SharedPtr); reference counting and atomic refcount overhead; copy vs. move semantics; passing by const reference (const MsgT&) or by value; intra-process communication and zero-copy message passing; unnecessary ownership transfer; const-correctness; rclcpp::SubscriptionOptions; performance cost of shared_ptr copies and atomic increments.

Key concepts: shared_ptr reference counting (thread-safe for copies, not for the pointed-to object); ROS 2 intra-process communication sharing one message instance among subscribers via shared_ptr; const vs non-const message access; data races and undefined behavior from concurrent writes; copy-on-write or cloning the message; callback groups, MutuallyExclusive vs Reentrant execution; multi-threaded executors; std::shared_ptr<const T> for read-only sharing; mutexes for synchronization.

Relevant concepts: data races and race conditions; shared mutable state; shared_ptr reference counting being thread-safe for ownership but not for the pointed-to object; const shared_ptr<const T> for read-only sharing; copy-on-write or deep copy; mutexes and locking; intra-process zero-copy messages; ROS 2 callback groups, MutuallyExclusive vs Reentrant executors; message lifetime and immutability.

Key concepts: MoveIt's MoveGroupInterface::plan and its helper constructMotionPlanRequest, which builds a moveit_msgs MotionPlanRequest. Relevant terms include move_group_interface.cpp (in moveit_ros_planning_interface/move_group_interface), goal constraints, position and orientation constraints, joint constraints, tolerances, PoseTarget and JointTarget, end effector links, workspace parameters, planner ID, planning pipeline, and num_planning_attempts.

Nav2 action client concepts: the NavigateToPose action (nav2_msgs/action/NavigateToPose), rclcpp_action::Client, send_goal and async_send_goal with goal response callbacks, goal handles, feedback and result callbacks, GoalStatus states (ACCEPTED, EXECUTING, SUCCEEDED, ABORTED, CANCELED), PoseStamped goal in map frame, rclcpp Node spinning, TurtleBot4 Navigation launch, and Nav2 BasicNavigator alternative.

Key concepts: ROS 2 action clients (rclcpp_action), the NavigateToPose action type (nav2_msgs::action::NavigateToPose), its goal, result, and feedback types, and the nested result wrapper rclcpp_action::ClientGoalHandle::WrappedResult containing a result code (SUCCEEDED, ABORTED, CANCELED, UNKNOWN), a goal ID, and the typed result response, plus the shared_future and result callback APIs used to retrieve it.

Relevant concepts: rclcpp_action WrappedResult struct with fields `code` (rclcpp_action::ResultCode: SUCCEEDED, ABORTED, CANCELED, UNKNOWN), `result` (action-specific result message), and `goal_id`. ResultCode indicates whether the goal completed successfully, was aborted by the server, canceled, or ended with an unknown state. Callback status checks, Nav2 NavigateToPose result, goal handle, and ROS 2 action client semantics.

Key concepts: ROS 2 action semantics, goal/feedback/result messages, action server goal states (accepted, executing, canceling, succeeded, canceled, aborted), result code (rclcpp_action::ResultCode SUCCEEDED, CANCELED, ABORTED, UNKNOWN), separation of status from result payload, asynchronous result futures, get_result_async, goal handle lifecycle, and designing result messages for application data versus lifecycle reporting.

A relevant guide would cover the python-can library's core concepts: Bus objects and interfaces (SocketCAN, Vector, PCAN, Kvaser, virtual), channels and bitrates, Message objects (arbitration ID, data bytes, DLC, extended/standard frames, timestamps), sending and receiving (send, recv, Notifier, Listener), message filters, logging and log file formats, and CAN bus configuration via the Bus constructor or config files.

PCAN-USB support in python-can: the interface is selected via bus type "pcan" and channel (e.g., PCAN_USBBUS1), requiring the PEAK PCAN-Basic driver/API library installed. Key concepts: bus interface type (e.g., "pcan", "socketcan", "vector"), channel identifier (e.g., "PCAN_USBBUS1", "can0"), bitrate (bits per second, such as 500000), and configuration methods: constructor arguments in Bus(), environment variables, and config files (~/.canrc, /etc/can.conf). Also covers the interface-specific parameters, fd settings, and verifying with tools like bus state or candump.

Key concepts for a relevant document: LiDAR driver packages (e.g., ouster-ros, velodyne_driver), ROS2 nodes and topics, sensor_msgs/PointCloud2 message format, packet parsing and decoding, UDP network configuration, frame IDs and TF transforms, Python or C++ SDK bindings, QoS settings, launch files, and rosbag recording for testing.

Key concepts: open-source ROS2 LiDAR drivers, driver architecture (SensorInterface, packet parsing, decoders), hardware-specific adaptation, packet formats and UDP/Ethernet networking, IP/port configuration, calibration files and sensor models, point cloud message types (sensor_msgs/PointCloud2), frame IDs and TF transforms, launch files and parameters, data processors and filtering, rebuilding with colcon, and supported vendors and SDK compatibility.

Key concepts: ROS 2 package management, apt and dpkg package removal (apt remove/purge), libbehaviortree-cpp-dev and behaviortree_cpp packages, version conflicts between system-installed and source-built BehaviorTree.CPP, CMake find_package, colcon workspace builds, rosdep dependency resolution, /usr/local/lib and /opt/ros install prefixes, stale CMake config files, ldconfig library cache, and rebuilding with rosdep install.

Key concepts: apt purge versus remove, residual configuration files, dpkg status and package database cleanup, apt autoremove and autoclean, clearing cached .deb packages, sourcing and rebuilding ROS workspaces, removing stale CMake config files (BehaviorTreeCPP cmake exports in /opt/ros or /usr/local), colcon build cleanup (rm -rf build install log), rosdep dependency resolution, and reinstalling via apt or source with matching version.

Relevant concepts: dpkg package database (/var/lib/dpkg/status, info/*.list, info/*.conffiles), conffiles tracking, package states (config-files "rc" state, purged vs removed), dpkg --purge, dpkg -L/-S to list and locate files, debsums or dpkg --verify to check file integrity, and orphaned files left in /etc or /usr/local, plus apt-get autoremove, dpkg-query, and ament/rosdep leftovers.

Gazebo splits into gzserver (headless physics, sensors, plugins, world simulation) and gzclient (the Qt-based GUI that renders and visualizes the server's state via transport messages). Running them separately lets simulations run headless, on remote or CI machines, without a display, and lets clients connect or disconnect. In C++ plugins, GUI plugins are loaded in gzclient, while server-side code runs in

The /usr/bin/gazebo launcher is a wrapper script that starts gzserver (physics and simulation server) and gzclient (GUI) together, handling argument parsing, plugin loading, and the gazebo master connection via gazebo::setupServer or environment variables, plus process lifecycle management such as launching the client after the server and shutting both down together.

Gazebo server-client communication relies on the transport library (Gazebo Transport, built on Protobuf messages and ZeroMQ/ Boost-based pub-sub) with topics, publishers, subscribers, and nodes. Key concepts include the gazebo::transport namespace, message types in gazebo::msgs, the master discovery service, and the gzserver/gzclient split. Customization involves modifying topic names, message handlers, or plugins, and rebuilding from source.

Gazebo launcher internals: the gazebo script/binary (gui and server launch via gazebo command, gzserver and gzclient executables), fork/exec of child processes, command-line arguments and flags (--verbose, -s, --gui-client, --server-only), environment variables like GAZEBO_MASTER_URI and GAZEBO_MODEL_PATH, the Gazebo transport/master messaging layer, process lifecycle and shutdown coordination via signals, and the gazebo.cc/gui.cc/server.cc source files.

Key concepts: gzserver (headless simulation backend) and gzclient (GUI frontend) as separate processes; the gazebo launcher that spawns both; the gazebo::Server and gazebo::client C++ APIs (gazebo::setupServer, gazebo::run, gazebo::shutdown); transport/communication via gazebo::transport nodes and topics; process lifecycle and shutdown coordination; command-line arguments and fork/exec launching; and headless versus GUI mode in embedded C++ programs.

Gazebo Garden system plugins, specifically the PosePublisher system plugin (gz::sim::systems::PosePublisher) attached to a model or link in SDF. Key terms: publish_link_pose, publish_sensor_pose, publish_nested_model_pose, publish_model_pose, update_frequency, static_publisher, and the gz-transport topic /model/<name>/pose. ROS integration via ros_gz_bridge (parameter_bridge) mapping gz.msgs.Pose_V to geometry_msgs/PoseArray or tf2 messages, plus RGBD camera sensor (depth camera, rgbd_camera) frames.

Key concepts: the Gazebo `pose_publisher` system plugin (libgz-sim-pose-publisher-system) and its SDF configuration within the `<plugin>` element of the world or model. Relevant tags include `<publish_link_pose>`, `<publish_nested_model_pose>`, `<publish_sensor_pose>`, `<publish_collision_pose>`, `<publish_visual_pose>`, `<publish_model_pose>`, `<update_frequency>`, and `<static_publisher>`. Also covered: the sensor `<topic>`, `<gz_frame_id>`, ros_gz_bridge mapping of Gazebo pose topics to ROS tf2 or geometry_msgs/PoseStamped.

Key concepts: Gazebo Garden pose publisher system plugin (gz::sim::systems::PosePublisher), SDF `<plugin>` configuration within `<model>`/`<sensor>`, boolean flags like publish_sensor_pose, publish_model_pose, publish_nested_model_pose, publish_collision_pose, publish_visual_pose, update_frequency, and static tags; gz-transport topics bridged to ROS 2 via ros_gz_bridge (geometry_msgs/PoseStamped or tf2 messages); custom plugin development with gz-sim C++ API, ISystemConfigure, ISystemPostUpdate, and entity components.
